chapters.title: The House of Flowers
chapters.intro: Day One. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Can ask; misses most of the answer
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Evelyn used to teach literature. Isabel's family has owned this lovely hotel for years. The foundation on the flyer is familiar from the office.

**What I wonder:** Whether Nate's definition of “a little spicy” will improve. Must remember the beach bar.

chapters.title: A Familiar Face
chapters.intro: Days Two and Three. Spanish in order of encounter.
evidence: I heard Tomás ask this, but I don't know the meaning yet.
Tomás said this while talking to Isabel. I didn't catch the meaning.
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Clara is Evelyn's daughter. Mariana has a lovely hummingbird tattoo she doesn't want her parents to know about. Isabel took a small silver key from Tomás.

**What I wonder:** Whether Clara is enjoying her visit as much as she'd hoped. Also, why does that bakery have to be so far from our hotel?

chapters.title: Things Best Left Alone
chapters.spanishTitle: Cosas que es mejor dejar en paz
chapters.intro: Wednesday, Day Four. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Works out ahora from the familiar después and the paper bag
Now? The question from Chapter Two made sense when the woman at the bakery offered to pack Nate's pastry now or later.
aunt. Tomás explained this today. I had heard it when Isabel and Tomás were discussing the key. I still haven't worked out *pero*.
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Graham helped Clara's family when her father died. Charles intends to send a statement to a solicitor tomorrow. Evelyn wanted them to do something together instead. Lucía has written about New Horizons before.

**What I wonder:** What made Clara so unhappy at the reception? I hope she and Evelyn manage to talk. Nate and I have a new beach to explore tomorrow.

chapters.title: A Change of Plans
chapters.intro: Thursday, Day Five. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Understands Isabel's gesture; meaning confirmed by context
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Charles Whitmore died this morning. Diego says he witnessed a push and heard Charles say, “You promised me she would never have to read it.” He could not identify the other person. Diego saw Charles with the repaired leather case earlier. He told the police. I told Inspector Salazar what I heard yesterday and what Graham said about intending to meet Charles today but not seeing him.

**What I wonder:** Who was Charles speaking about? Was his disagreement with Evelyn connected to what happened? I hope Diego has someone to talk to.

chapters.title: Beyond the Hotel
chapters.intro: Friday, Day Six. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Understands after the price is written down
Dos vasos de agua, por favor
Yes, but it takes a little while
Waiter explains; recognizes un poco from Chapter One
I don't want to talk about that
Recognizes part; Mariana supplies full meaning
But. The waiter explained that the fish would take a little while.
But, Aunt… I can finally understand what Tomás was saying to Isabel in Chapter Two.
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** The foundation's public display shows a woman with Mariana's tattoo and face. It claims her birthmark was entirely cleared six months ago. Mariana still has a visible mark. She did not want to discuss the photograph. Graham had a leather case with a repaired handle like the one Charles carried.

**What I wonder:** Is there an innocent explanation for the photograph? Lucía may know something about the foundation's earlier publicity. I will not press Mariana.

chapters.title: An Old Acquaintance
chapters.intro: Saturday, Day Seven. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Infers the question from the papers and Rosa's actions; Tomás confirms
Understands retrospectively after Tomás explains the cupboard
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Lucía obtained the earlier original photograph and showed me that the two images on the foundation display come from the same picture. The supposed after image was altered. This does not establish whether Mariana received treatment. Rosa used the silver key for the event-supplies cupboard. Evelyn seems to regret something about the past.

**What I wonder:** Who decided to use the altered photograph, and why? Does the foundation's dishonesty have anything to do with Charles's death, or are these separate matters?

chapters.title: Between Friends
chapters.intro: Sunday, Day Eight. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: This one has sugar. This one doesn't
Recognizes azúcar and infers the contrast; shopkeeper confirms
I prefer this one, without sugar
Es más tranquilo por la mañana
Reuses the Chapter Six question independently
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Clara says Graham promised her and Evelyn that she would never have to read her father's papers. I told Salazar about the promise with Clara's permission. Mariana remembers Graham carrying the leather case on Friday. Edward admitted in a letter to signing documents he knew were wrong, but denied taking some missing money, according to Clara.

**What I wonder:** Was Charles speaking about Clara when Diego heard him? Did someone make a promise to Charles as well?
travelTips: **Prefiero este…** — I prefer this one. Point to your choice, then explain why or add a preference.
**Sin azúcar** — without sugar. The pattern *sin* plus an ingredient is useful when ordering food or drinks.
Listen for contrasts such as *este tiene… este no*. You may understand the choice even if you miss a word.

chapters.title: A Day of Errands
chapters.intro: Monday, Day Nine. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Uses a traveler-sheet expression to clarify a reply
This one is stronger / more durable
Understands from demonstration and Nate's suggestion
Uses politely to question a price
Infers from the label, pointing and later explanation
Is it included in the price?
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Evelyn says she and Charles intended to disclose past wrongdoing, but disagreed about doing it together. Lucía has confirmed foundation payments to businesses connected to a criminal investigation. Graham returned the repaired case to Evelyn and said he had kept it with him since Wednesday evening. I told Salazar about the discrepancy with Diego's Thursday sighting. Evelyn intends to give evidence at Thursday's trustee meeting and has independent advice and copies with her solicitor. She says a letter Charles sent after Edward died records Graham's assurance that Clara wouldn't need to read the papers.

**What I wonder:** Why would Graham say he had kept the case since Wednesday if Charles still had it Thursday? Does he have an explanation I haven't considered?
travelTips: **Creo que hay un error.** This is a polite way to raise a concern without accusing someone.
**¿Está incluido en el precio?** Use this when checking whether a service, charge or extra item is included.
**¿Puede repetirlo más despacio, por favor?** Ask for a slower reply before giving up on a conversation. A gesture, label or written number can help you understand the answer.

chapters.title: Another Morning
chapters.intro: Tuesday, Day Ten. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Is it all right like this?
Understands from shopkeeper showing the repair
Dos cafés, por favor. Y uno sin azúcar
Two coffees, please. And one without sugar
Combines familiar ordering and ingredient patterns
Infers from familiar más and ordering context
I don't know what to do
Recognizes no sé; Tomás explains full meaning
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Evelyn said she had changed her mind when she woke up this morning and wanted Clara to have Edward's original letter. Clara wasn't ready to take it. Rosa heard a disagreement about the letter, saw a man leave and found Evelyn injured. She did not see the injury happen. Rosa told the police, and I told Salazar what I personally heard at breakfast. Evelyn died at the hospital. Graham said he had not spoken to her today. Nate and I have moved to another hotel and provided our contact information.

**What I wonder:** Who was Evelyn arguing with? I hope Clara has the support she needs. Nothing else seems particularly important tonight.
travelTips: **¿Algo más?** is a common follow-up when ordering or shopping. Listen for it rather than assuming the conversation is finished.
**Eso es todo** is a useful way to finish an order.
**Lo siento mucho** expresses sympathy. A short, sincere phrase can be more appropriate than trying to say something complicated.

vocabulary: Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Also **¿Pica mucho?** — Is it very spicy?
Una mesa para dos, por favor.
Also **¿Cuánto es?** — How much is it? Useful for asking the total at checkout.
travelers.tip: Tip: Learn nouns with their articles. **El hotel** means “the hotel”; **la llave** means “the key.” For grammar explanations, examples, and pronunciation practice, use the companion app.
